candidates.tagline: Designed in 1962 to make jetways obsolete — Dulles's mobile lounge is STILL here
candidates.story: Dulles Airport's 1962 terminal was designed with no jetways at all, relying instead on 'mobile lounges' — massive tarmac buses on hydraulic legs — that ferry passengers to parked planes; it made Dulles the only major airport in the world without jetways, and after 60 years of universal passenger hatred, Trump just announced a $22.5B renovation to finally remove them.
candidates.why_funny: Every other airport on Earth chose jetways in the 1960s; Dulles chose enormous motorised bus-tanks, then kept using them while every traveller complained for six decades.
candidates.alt: Front-on view of a Dulles Airport mobile lounge — a huge boxy vehicle on hydraulic legs approaching the terminal across the tarmac

candidates.tagline: TECNO's '0mm bezel' phone has a lip that snags your thumb on every swipe — because bezels existed for a reason
candidates.story: TECNO's concept phone, unveiled at IFA 2026 on September 3, 2026, claims 'literally zero display border — not 1mm, not 0.5mm, zero' by raising the metal frame slightly above the screen surface, but hands-on testing found users' fingers catch on the raised lip with every edge swipe gesture — the exact problem bezels were designed to prevent.
candidates.why_funny: They eliminated the visible bezel and replaced it with an invisible physical lip that catches your thumb even more — and the official fix is adding a screen protector, which is just a bezel with extra steps.
candidates.alt: Person holding the TECNO Borderless Concept phone, its 6.7-inch display appearing to run fully edge-to-edge with no visible border around the screen
